quarterly_data.signal: CFO Lorenzo Grandi on the AI data-center mix: the connectivity flow (silicon photonics, microcontrollers and BiCMOS EICs for optical transceivers) generates the strongest revenue, and for 2027 ST expects 'mostly of our revenue will be in MDRF for around 80% of the billing' with only 20% in APMS (thermal and power flows). ST is 'marginal today' in data-center power and is building its portfolio for the 800V architecture, expecting 'meaningful revenue after 2028 for the power'. Silicon photonics is described as accretive to the gross-margin target. For NPO/CPO, ST says it has 'all the ingredients', including packaging, and the timing will be driven by customers.
quarterly_data.figure: around 80% of 2027 data-center billing in MDRF (connectivity), 20% in APMS; power meaningful revenue after 2028

quarterly_data.signal: Silicon-photonics customers are asking for long-term agreements that lock 'capacity, volumes, pricing, and also with cash advance for many of these agreements that we are signing'; the LTAs cover 'more than one year, two, three years'. ST says it must invest to follow demand, using its 300mm infrastructure, and that the silicon-photonics capacity is fungible with other technologies such as microcontrollers. More broadly, 'we are facing backlog and demand that is well above our ability to serve the market', with the backlog extending 'well inside 2027'; industrial lead times for some products are 'now reaching 50 weeks', and microcontroller distribution inventory is well below the normal 12-13 weeks. A Q2 hiccup at the Singapore fab was escalated immediately by automotive customers.
quarterly_data.figure: industrial lead times reaching 50 weeks; silicon-photonics LTAs with cash advances covering two, three years; distribution inventory below normal 12-13 weeks

quarterly_data.signal: Gross-margin bridge from the 37% Q3 guide: around 70 basis points of unloading charges that will fade, around 50 basis points of reshaping duplication cost that will be 'very marginal' by mid next year, and 'more than 400 basis points' from closing two old 200mm fabs and two 150mm silicon-carbide fabs, which comes as a step function 'at the end of 2027, beginning of 2028', depending on customer qualification in the new fabs. ST says its own part of the plan (capacity, process transfer, product duplication) is done and it is now sampling customers. APMS (where silicon carbide is a large part) is expected back to profitability at the end of next year, early 2028.
quarterly_data.figure: more than 400 basis points GM uplift from closing two 200mm and two 150mm SiC fabs, end of 2027 / early 2028

quarterly_data.signal: Pricing: with backlog and demand higher than capacity, ST is raising prices by more than its input-cost increases ('not in a way that is too much opportunistic'); average pricing in 2026 will be 'substantially flattish, slightly increasing' (engaged-customer contracts limit increases, while MCU STM32 and some analog in distribution are easier to reprice). 2027 pricing is not yet being negotiated, but this year's increases stay and 2027 is expected to be 'stable, slightly increasing'.
quarterly_data.figure: 2026 average pricing substantially flattish, slightly increasing; 2027 stable, slightly increasing

quarterly_data.signal: Silicon carbide: capacity (still at 150mm) is the limiting factor while demand recovers, especially at European car makers. SiC revenue will grow double digit this year, and with the programs in hand ST sees SiC revenue next year 'back at EUR 1.01 billion'; the move to 200mm (Catania, and Chongqing in China) should significantly improve profitability, and ST is introducing Generation 4 and Generation 5. Satellite: the business is 'reaching closely EUR 1 billion'; with Starlink/SpaceX ST holds 'around 90% of market share', which management calls not sustainable as second sources arrive, but new entrants are already being shipped to; cumulative revenue over the next three years 'well above EUR 3 billion'.
quarterly_data.figure: SiC revenue next year back at EUR 1.01 billion; satellite business closely EUR 1 billion; around 90% share at Starlink/SpaceX
